subject: Customer-scoped log mapping and timestamp sampling for SIG/CAIQ
messages:
From: Samira Qureshi <samira@polaris-analytics.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Liu <peter@polaris-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Mapping of aggregated logs to tenant retention windows (SIG/CAIQ ask)

Hi Michael,

Thanks for taking this — Polaris is working through our SIG/CAIQ assessment and the security team has a couple of questions about how Redwood maps aggregated inference logs to retention windows for tenant-scoped data. Two specific asks: 

1) We see that you store multiple telemetry tiers (request traces, anonymized tokens, system events). For SOC 2 evidence we need a mapping that shows which telemetry types are persisted at the tenant level vs platform-aggregated only, and the exact TTLs (e.g., 30d/90d/365d) applied.

2) For debugging-sensitive cases, we need to understand how timestamp sampling works when logs are aggregated: do you sample events before or after tenant-sharding? Is there any cross-tenant aggregation that would prevent us from certifying deletion?

Attached a CSV with a sample mapping we started. Can you confirm Redwood's authoritative mapping and any compensating controls (keystore separation, audit hooks, escrow?) that would be included in the SIG response?

Appreciate a short write-up we can include in the control narrative.

—Samira

Attachment: polaris_log_sample_map.csv (CSV stub, columns: telemetry_type, tenant_persisted, retention_days, sample_note)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@polaris-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping of aggregated logs to tenant retention windows (SIG/CAIQ ask)

Samira —

Thanks for the clear CSV, that helps. Short answer up front: tenant-identifiable logs (request metadata, full request/response traces when customer enables debug) are stored per-tenant with tenant-scoped TTLs; aggregated telemetry (system metrics, anonymized model telemetry) is stored at platform level and cannot be back-traced to a tenant. Sampling is performed after tenant-scoping for tenant logs (we do not mix tenant identifiers into platform aggregates).

I'll draft a control narrative and pull in Naomi (compliance) and Karthik (product) to confirm keystore/escrow language. Expect a 1–2 page reply with a sample mapping and references to CAIQ entries (I/O-C-2, I/O-C-7).

Quick notes: 
- Tenant-scoped TTLs are configurable per-contract; default for debug traces is 90d, for standard request metadata 30d.
- Keystore separation: tenant encryption keys are derived from a customer KMS when requested (we have an HSM-backed option).
- Audit hooks: deletion is logged to a write-once audit stream tied to the tenant id and retained for our SOC 2 evidence (non-repudiable).

I will follow up with the narrative and PDFs.

Best,
Michael Grant
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_keystore_retention_matrix.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Samira Qureshi <samira@polaris-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping of aggregated logs to tenant retention windows (SIG/CAIQ ask)

Hi all — looping in the compliance artifacts team. Michael's summary is accurate; below is language we recommend for the SIG/CAIQ control narrative. Please treat this as the authoritative text you can paste into the questionnaire with minor edits for your environment.

---
Control narrative (draft):
Redwood Inference classifies telemetry into three tiers: tenant-scoped traces (includes request/response payloads when debug logging is enabled), tenant-scoped metadata (non-sensitive request headers, routing, timestamps), and platform-aggregated metrics (system telemetry and model performance aggregates). Tenant-scoped traces and metadata are stored in per-tenant partitions and are subject to configurable TTLs set at contract provisioning. By default, tenant-scoped traces: 90 days; tenant metadata: 30 days. Platform-aggregated metrics are stored separately and do not contain tenant identifiers; these metrics are retained for 365 days for product analytics and capacity planning.

Deletion and verification: tenant-scoped data is deleted according to TTL, and deletions generate an audit event recorded in an immutable audit log. When customers request earlier erasure, Redwood performs a tenant-scoped purge and supplies a signed deletion certificate describing the object keys removed and the timestamp.

Sampling and aggregation: Sampling for telemetry used in platform-wide analytics is applied after tenant identifiers have been removed. No sampling operation aggregates raw tenant identifiers into platform metrics.

Compensating controls and key management: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed keys. For customers using CMK, data-at-rest encryption is tenant-specific; we store only encrypted blobs and do not retain plaintext decryption keys.

---

I'll attach a short mapping table and the CAIQ/SIG mapping row numbers after Karthik confirms the product details.

Cheers,
Naomi
Director, Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@polaris-analytics.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-30T13:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping of aggregated logs to tenant retention windows (SIG/CAIQ ask)

Samira, Michael — quick technical clarifications to add to Naomi's narrative: 

1) Partitioning: tenant-scoped objects are physically partitioned by tenant id and logical shard. Purge operations are index-driven — we remove keys by partition and record the operation id in the immutable audit stream.

2) Sampling: for performance telemetry used in capacity planning, we perform reservoir sampling on anonymized events (post-hash of tenant id) with a deterministic salt that prevents reconstruction. We consider this pseudonymized, not tenant-identifiable.

3) Escrow/forensics: for customers requiring long-term forensic retention we offer a log-escrow addendum; retained artifacts are exported to a customer-controlled storage location and are out-of-band from platform aggregates.

If you want, I can add two example SIG rows mapping (I/O-6 -> tenant metadata retention, I/O-12 -> deletion certificate process).

-Karthik
Product Manager, Data Platform | Redwood Inference
